claims.note: In dollars the fitted floor binds in-sample for eps < 0.0158 and the realized quality of every fitted rule falls 0.0033-0.0090 below its in-sample value (selection of the argmax on probing plus split shift), so the binding eps-rules satisfy their own floor in only 11-32% of resamples and the unconstrained rule at eps = 0.02 in about half; the bootstrap sd of E[V]-vbar is about 0.007, so even without shift a floor that binds exactly is met in about 50% of resamples. Refitting at a smaller eps (a safety margin of 0.015-0.03, table 2) restores >= 95%. In seconds the unconstrained optimum improves quality, the floor is slack and is satisfied in 100% of resamples. The theorem is a statement about expectations under known primitives; this measures the estimation gap, not a failure of the theorem.
